findings.issue: `posSemidef_charFun_star_kernel_of_star_eq_neg : Matrix.PosSemidef (fun a b : E => charFun μ (a + star b))` is exactly `(charFun_isPositiveDefinite_of_star_eq_neg hstar).posSemidef` — the same file proves `charFun_isPositiveDefinite_of_star_eq_neg` at line 63 and `IsPositiveDefinite.posSemidef` (PositiveDefinite/Basic.lean:184) states `Matrix.PosSemidef (fun a b => F (a + star b))` under the same `[AddMonoid]`/`[StarAddMonoid]` hypotheses. The PR re-proves it from `posSemidef_charFun` instead, and it has no in-repository users.

summary: The migration now reuses Mathlib's arbitrary-index `Matrix.PosSemidef` API correctly and leaves no shadow predicate, but three redundant declarations/derivations remain: two call sites pull back with `.submatrix` what `posSemidef_charFun` already supplies for an arbitrary index family, and two thin wrappers (`IsPositiveDefinite.posSemidef_gram`, `posSemidef_charFun_star_kernel_of_star_eq_neg`) are now exactly `Matrix.PosSemidef.submatrix` and `IsPositiveDefinite.posSemidef` with no in-repo users.
